clue.text: Home fixture for City

definitions.meaning: a tub plumbed into a house is one of its fixed fittings
the Somerset spa city with its Roman remains and Georgian crescents

explanation.walkthrough: 'Home fixture' sounds like a football match played at home; it is a piece of household plumbing. The city is in Somerset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the washing tub in a house and the English spa city.

clue.text: Graduate's late in this sham condition

parts.note: a graduate is a BA, Bachelor of Arts, with the 's adding S
someone late is tardy

explanation.surface: A graduate turns up late to some fraudulent arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sham condition' points to illegitimate birth, an old sense of 'spurious' being 'born out of wedlock'.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegitimacy of birth was called a spurious, or sham, status in older usage.

clue.text: Lifting the foot that is shorter

parts.note: the word foot in its shortened form is the abbreviation FT

explanation.surface: Someone raises the foot, the shorter one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifting' looks like raising a foot; it is slang for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is informal for stealing, a crime of taking property.

clue.text: Standard fails badly in Wagner work

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of fails are put in a wrong, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A standard performance goes wrong in a Wagner opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's last music drama, about the Grail knight, is named for its hero.

clue.text: Speech in the house

definitions.meaning: a formal talk delivered to an audience
where someone lives, as written on an envelope

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a speech in the House of Commons; 'in' is only a link between two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a formal oration and the location of a dwelling for letters.

clue.text: Instruction to players-lay on line!

parts.note: to lay on an event is to stage it
a line one follows is a direction

explanation.surface: Actors are told to put on their lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes in a script tell the actors where to move and how to act.

clue.text: Get unfair treatment as ballerina with no solo parts?

indicators.note: treatment here means the letters of get unfair are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A corps dancer complains of being treated unfairly with no solos.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps de ballet dancer who performs only in groups, never alone.

clue.text: Doh in the French style of stringed instrument

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other here

parts.note: le is the French for the
UT was the old solfa name for the first note, now doh

explanation.surface: A note played in the French manner on a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the original name, in medieval solfa, of the note now called doh. 'style of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked, pear-shaped instrument with strings, popular in Renaissance music.

clue.text: It happens price is affected in the training period

indicators.note: affected signals that the letters of the words before it are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Whatever the cost, the price of training is affected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link: the fodder is IT HAPPENS PRICE, fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning a trade under a master craftsman takes a fixed term of years.

clue.text: Popular team incarcerated

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A popular team is locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in prison is informally said to be in jail, behind bars.

clue.text: Night drug, please, to be made up

definitions.text: Night drug, please, to be made up

indicators.note: to be made up means the letters of the words before are put together afresh, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient asks for a night-time medicine to be prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose of medicine taken to induce slumber, which a pharmacist makes up.

clue.text: Heavenly time!

parts.note: a time spent in heaven, the existence that follows death, rather than a lovely time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly time' sounds like a wonderful party; read literally it is time spent in heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Life after death is spent, many believe, in heaven.

clue.text: Leicester undeveloped, almost?

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: at an immature stage, not yet grown, is early

explanation.surface: Leicester has yet to develop, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester is not the city here but the title: Robert Dudley, Elizabeth I's favourite, was its earl.
explanation.definitionFit: The title held by Robert Dudley and others is a peerage of that rank.

clue.text: Government department feed NEC badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of feed NEC are mixed into a wrong order

explanation.surface: A ministry feeds the National Executive Committee poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ministry of Defence is a government department that runs the armed forces.

clue.text: Some paving the way in fog-lane, maybe

indicators.note: in places the way within the jumbled letters
maybe suggests fog-lane is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: The way through a foggy lane might be paved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some paving' is the definition: a single slab is only part of a paved surface. 'maybe' marks the anagram and 'in' the insertion; 'the way' is the usual crossword street.
explanation.definitionFit: Paving is made of large flat slabs of stone laid as a path.

clue.text: Twiggy's pub in divine situation

definitions.note: read as what Twiggy is: the 1960s model was famous for being very thin

indicators.note: in places the pub within the heavens

parts.note: heaven, where the divine are situated, is the sky
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Twiggy's local is a heavenly place.
explanation.walkthrough: Twiggy was a famously slender 1960s English fashion model; 'Twiggy's' means 'Twiggy is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The model was known for a thin, bony figure, like a twig.

clue.text: Test, rain affected, is put into difficulties

indicators.note: affected signals that the letters of test and rain are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket Test is hit by rain and runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, which rain can spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict or bring into hardship, as in reduced, straitened circumstances.

clue.text: Ingredient of hummus, a thin mixture, put before one

indicators.note: put before places the jumbled letters ahead of the next piece
mixture signals that the letters of a thin are stirred into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A recipe step: make a thin mixture of a hummus ingredient first.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seed paste is blended with chickpeas to make hummus.

clue.text: Ask earnestly for fairytales

definitions.meaning: stories of mischievous sprites, imps, make up their lore

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: an imp is a small fairy and lore is its tales, so the word splits as IMP and LORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech or beg; and split, the folklore of little devils.

clue.text: Party-leader feel bitter these days?

parts.note: the leading letter of party is P
to resent is to feel bitter

explanation.surface: A party leader is aggrieved at modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: The time now, nowadays, as opposed to past or future.

clue.text: Youth, for example, lies about

indicators.note: about means the letters of lies are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Young people often tell lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth' is not young people: the Isle of Youth is an island off Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Youth is an island belonging to Cuba.

clue.text: Severely criticise a bank-cashier, say, with a cigar

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: say means the word for the cashier is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a bank cashier is a teller

explanation.surface: A customer berates a bank clerk while smoking a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin cigar, open at the end that is lit.

clue.text: Oriel floundering in river

indicators.note: floundering signals that the letters of Oriel struggle into a new order

explanation.surface: An Oriel College oarsman flounders in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is an Oxford college, which suggests rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river in France, flowing to the Atlantic past Orleans and Nantes.

clue.text: Weekly pay unopened for a very long time?

indicators.note: unopened means the opening letter of the word is not there

parts.note: wages are weekly pay

explanation.surface: The weekly pay packet sits unopened for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a great while, as in waiting a long while.

clue.text: One takes all the time in the world

definitions.text: One takes all the time in the world

parts.words: One takes all the time in the world
parts.note: a scientist who dates the Earth's rocks takes, that is measures, all of the planet's time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes all the time in the world' sounds like someone very slow; 'takes' means measures, and the world's time is its geological age.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who measures the age of rocks and of the Earth.

clue.text: Destination, having driven in the Cotswolds?

definitions.text: Destination, having driven in the Cotswolds?

parts.words: Destination, having driven in the Cotswolds?
parts.note: where flocks driven along country lanes end up, not where a motorist goes

explanation.walkthrough: The Cotswolds are hills in western England famed for sheep farming; 'driven' means herded, not motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure where a farmer keeps a flock after herding them in.

clue.text: Bird in the water, naturally

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird is naturally in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird related to the gull, with a forked tail.
